messages:
jordan: FYI I opened this thread to collect the post-incident follow-ups and a short exec-facing brief we can share with the customer tomorrow. Incident window: 1998-12-05T02:04:16Z -> ~02:07:00Z. Impact: brief degradation of inference throughput for ~3m, some requests timed out and were retried by customers.

incident-bot: Pager duty incident created: INC-1998. Priority: P1. On-call: jordan. Initial alert at 1998-12-05T02:04:15Z.

jordan: Quick summary from on-call — root cause looks like a kernel regression in the runtime that caused a double-free under a specific quantization codepath. We fell back to previous model variant quickly but some in-flight reqs failed.

mira: Thanks. I collected logs and put the low-level pointer/freed stack traces in the incident artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-1998/artifacts/kernel-trace.log

sam: Customer reports: two enterprise customers (AcmeData, BrightBank) saw elevated error rates and auto-retries. Support opened tickets: #ACME-402, #BB-785. Acme saw ~0.6% failed requests for 3.5 minutes; BrightBank had ~1.2% for ~2.5 minutes. Both asked for an RCA and timeline.

clare: Ops notes from bridge: we enabled fallback routing to dedicated pool at 02:05:10Z which mitigated new traffic. We also disabled the problematic quantization profile temporarily. Canary-migration scheduled at 03:30Z to roll kernel patch.

jordan: Action list I want tracked and owners assigned: 1) Root-cause fix + test coverage (mira), 2) Postmortem doc + timeline (jordan), 3) Customer exec brief + status page update (danielle), 4) Backfill tests in CI for quantization profiles (mira), 5) Update runbooks for fallback routing (clare).

mira: I can take 1 and 4. I already have a repro with a minimal model; will add unit test and stress test. ETA for patch PR: today EOD.

clare: I'll do 5 — add clearer step for disabling quantization profiles and a checklist for verifying KV cache integrity. ETA: tomorrow morning.

danielle: I will draft the exec brief and statuspage copy. Can someone add the exact customer windows and affected endpoints? Sam, can you paste the customer timelines here?

sam: Acme timeline: spikes at 02:04:18Z, fail window until 02:07:50Z. BrightBank: spike at 02:05:00Z, resolved by 02:07:30Z. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embed for both customers.

danielle: Great. Here's the first pass of the exec-facing brief. Please review — short, non-technical, action-oriented.

```
Subject: Incident summary — brief degradation of inference service on Dec 5

Hi [Customer],

We want to let you know about a short service degradation that affected some inference requests on Dec 5 between ~02:04 and ~02:08 UTC. During this period a runtime regression caused an increased error rate for a subset of requests. Our automated fallback routing engaged and most traffic was routed to a stable pool within ~60s.

What happened: a kernel-level issue in an internal quantization path led to some in-flight requests failing.

What we did: we detected the anomaly via alerting and manually engaged fallback routing to a dedicated pool. We disabled the problematic quantization profile and deployed a regression patch to the runtime.

Customer impact: a small fraction of requests experienced failures and retries. If you saw increased error rates between 02:04 and 02:08 UTC, we recommend reviewing any automated retry logic for that period.

Next steps: we have a fix in development with tests and will deploy a canary patch today. We will share a full RCA with timeline and remediation steps within 48 hours.

If you want an expedited follow-up or a bridge with an engineer, reply and well schedule a session.

Best,
The Redwood Inference Reliability Team
```

jordan: Looks good. Two edits: remove the sentence about 'manual' engagement — we used the console but want to emphasize automated fallback. Also add a line: "No customer data was exposed at any time."

danielle: Updated draft with both edits. New version below.

```
Subject: Incident summary — brief degradation of inference service on Dec 5

Hi [Customer],

We want to let you know about a short service degradation that affected some inference requests on Dec 5 between ~02:04 and ~02:08 UTC. During this period a runtime regression caused an increased error rate for a subset of requests. Our automated fallback routing engaged and most traffic was routed to a stable pool within ~60s.

What happened: a kernel-level issue in an internal quantization path led to some in-flight requests failing.

What we did: we detected the anomaly via alerting, engaged fallback routing to a dedicated pool, disabled the problematic quantization profile and prepared a regression patch for rollout.

Customer impact: a small fraction of requests experienced failures and retries. If you saw increased error rates between 02:04 and 02:08 UTC, we recommend reviewing any automated retry logic for that period. No customer data was exposed at any time.

Next steps: we have a fix in development with tests and will deploy a canary patch today. We will share a full RCA with timeline and remediation steps within 48 hours.

If you want an expedited follow-up or a bridge with an engineer, reply and well schedule a session.

Best,
The Redwood Inference Reliability Team
```

mira: Thumbs up. Suggest adding a short technical annex to the full RCA that describes the quantization codepath and the kernel regression — keeps exec brief short but gives details in postmortem.

clare: Agree. Also add the mitigation checklist we used as an appendix when we share with customers — helps them trust our steps.

sam: For the status page update, propose this: "Degraded service for inference endpoints due to runtime regression; traffic successfully routed to fallback pool. Full RCA forthcoming." Short and to the point.

jordan: Approve. danielle, can you push the statuspage update now in draft? We'll wait on the full RCA before publishing final.

danielle: Drafted status page entry and saved to the incident folder. I also added the exec brief to the customer comms doc and linked the artifacts.

incident-bot: Task created: INC-1998-POSTMORTEM (assignee: jordan). Due: 48h.

jordan: I'll own the postmortem doc and timeline. I'll collect timestamps, add bridge transcript, and coordinate with mira for the technical annex. Expect first draft in 24h.

mira: Patch PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1209. Includes regression test and a stress script. Requesting review from eng-runtime.

clare: Can we add a follow-up action to validate fallback routing metrics and add an alert if fallback usage is >1% for >5m? That would have caught rising use earlier.

jordan: Good call. Adding as action item. clare assign to eng-sre for alert rule (clare to own).

danielle: Customer outreach plan: 1) Exec brief to customers today, 2) Offer bridge for impacted customers, 3) Full RCA and timeline within 48h, 4) Follow-up check-in in 7 days to confirm no regressions. Any objections?

sam: No objections. I'll coordinate with Acme and BrightBank on bridge times.

jordan: Okay team — solid plan. We'll reconvene after the first draft of postmortem. Thanks for moving fast on the patch and comms. :thumbsup:

mira: Night folks, continuing on patch and tests.

clare: I'll update runbooks in the morning and add the alert rule.

1998123620: (thread closed)
